sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Nothing. Talo Klao (Nifu, Sasstown) vowel inventory, ATR/[EXP] harmony and verb-suffix assimilation; tone explicitly set aside in fn. 3 ('The behavior of these suffixes with regard to tone requires further investigation'); the words stress/accent do not occur.
Consonant and vowel tables only (from Duitsman et al. 1975, Lightfoot 1974, Singler 1983); nothing on tone rules or stress.

sources.citation: Duitsman, John, Jana Bertkau and James Laesch. 1975. A survey of Kru dialects. Studies in African Linguistics 6(1): 77-103.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Sec. 4.4 Tone: 'Phonetically, there are three level tones and, in most dialects, at least one rising and at least one falling tone.. an amazing amount of tonal interaction between syllables' ('post-associated tones'); refers readers to Lightfoot, Tones on Kru Monosyllables, for Klae (Jlepe dialect).

sources.citation: Elimelech, Baruch. 1974. On the reality of underlying contour tones. In Ian Maddieson (ed.), The Tone Tome: Studies on Tone from the UCLA Tone Project (UCLA Working Papers in Phonetics 27), 74-83.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. 'Kru' = Nana Kru dialect: High, Low, Rising, Falling tones on monosyllables; only four melodies on disyllables (L-L, H-H, H-R, H-F), hence 'tone is a property of words in Kru and must therefore be represented by a suprasegmental matrix'; downdrift; R R -> H R simplification.
